contentBlocks.title: Alternative Income Source Detected — What to Do Next
contentBlocks.description: Did SASSA flag your grant with 'Alternative Income Source Detected'? Learn what triggered this status, how bank deposits affect your application, and step-by-step instructions to appeal the decision and secure your SRD grant.

contentBlocks.text: Alternative Income Source Detected — What It Means

The 'Alternative Income Source Detected' status is one of the most common reasons for SRD R370 grant declines. It means SASSA's automated monthly audit found evidence in their database that you have another source of financial support. This does not always mean you actually have income — system errors and misinterpreted bank transactions are very common.
This status affects SRD R370 applicants whose bank account deposits triggered SASSA's income detection threshold.

contentBlocks.explanation: SASSA cross-checks your ID against government databases (SARS, UIF, NSFAS, Department of Labour) and also scans your bank account transactions. If any system shows income, employment, or funding, your grant is declined for that month.
whyItHappens: You have an active UIF registration on the Department of Labour database (even if you no longer receive payments)
You are registered as an NSFAS-funded student (even if your studies are complete)
Your bank account received a deposit exceeding R624 in a single month
You are registered for PAYE tax through an employer
You are listed as receiving another social grant or pension
A family member transferred money to your account for groceries or emergencies
You transferred money between your own bank accounts
Someone else uses your bank account for their transactions
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: This status applies to each individual month. Even if you fix the issue, the next month is evaluated as a fresh cycle. You must appeal each declined month separately.
whatYouShouldDo: Check your bank statements for the month in question and identify every deposit
If you are unemployed but have UIF history, get a UI-19 termination letter from the Department of Labour
If you completed your studies, get an NSFAS cancellation letter from the myNSFAS portal
For each non-income deposit (gift, family transfer, loan repayment), write a sworn affidavit explaining the source
Submit an appeal on the DSD Appeal website at srd.dsd.gov.za for each declined month
Attach supporting documents: bank statements, affidavit, UIF letter, or NSFAS letter

contentBlocks.text: SASSA uses an automated bank verification system that scans your linked bank account every month. Any deposit — even a gift from a family member, a loan repayment, or money you transferred between your own accounts — can trigger this status if the total exceeds R624 in a calendar month.

contentBlocks.title: R624 Threshold
contentBlocks.text: The SRD R370 grant uses a strict means test threshold of R624 per month. If your bank account shows combined deposits exceeding R624 in any month, SASSA automatically flags 'Alternative Income Source' — even if the money is not actual income.
Common Scenarios That Trigger This Status

items: Family member sent you money for groceries or school fees
Friend repaid a loan they owed you
You transferred money from a savings account to your everyday account
Your employer paid you a final payout after retrenchment months ago
The Department of Labour still has your UIF status as 'active' even though you no longer receive UIF
Your former school or university still shows you as an active NSFAS student
Your spouse or partner deposits money into your account for household expenses

contentBlocks.text: How to Appeal 'Alternative Income Source' Declines
Appealing this status requires proving that the deposits in your account are not actual income. Follow these steps carefully:

steps.title: Review your bank statements
steps.description: Download or print your bank statements for the declined month(s). Highlight every deposit and note the source of each one.

steps.title: Prepare a sworn affidavit
steps.description: Visit your nearest SAPS station and write a sworn affidavit explaining each deposit. For example: 'R500 from my sister for my child's school fees — this is not income.' The affidavit must be commissioned by a police officer.

steps.title: Gather supporting evidence
steps.description: If UIF is the issue: get a UI-19 termination letter from the Department of Labour. If NSFAS is the issue: get a cancellation letter from the myNSFAS portal. If gifts: ask family members to write supporting letters.

steps.title: Submit your appeal online
steps.description: Go to srd.dsd.gov.za. Enter your ID number and phone number. Verify with the OTP sent to your phone. Select the declined month(s) and upload your affidavit, bank statements, and supporting letters.

steps.title: Wait for tribunal ruling
steps.description: The Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA) will review your case. Rulings typically take 60 to 90 days. If approved, you will receive backpay for all declined months.

faqs.question: My friend sent me R500 as a birthday gift. Will SASSA count this as income?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any deposit into your bank account, even a gift from family or friends, can trigger the 'Alternative Income Source' flag. You can appeal by providing a sworn affidavit from your friend confirming it was a gift.

faqs.question: How much money in deposits can trigger this status?
faqs.answer: Any single deposit over R624, or multiple smaller deposits totalling more than R624 in a calendar month, can trigger this status.

faqs.question: Do I need to appeal every month separately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because SASSA evaluates eligibility on a monthly basis, you must appeal for each individual month that shows 'Alternative Income Source'.

faqs.question: Can I transfer money between my own bank accounts?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it may trigger this status. If you transfer from savings to chequing, the deposit into the chequing account may be counted. Keep an affidavit explaining this ready.

faqs.question: How long does the appeal take?
faqs.answer: The ITSAA tribunal typically takes 60 to 90 days to issue a ruling. If successful, SASSA must pay all backdated amounts within 14 business days.
